settings_description: Most settings follow you to your other devices.
settings_new_sender_hint: Shows “First time writing to you” next to a sender you have never exchanged mail with and who isn’t in your contacts. Off, the app doesn’t search your mail for it.
settings_verified_badge_hint: Turn it on only if your mail server checks all mail, including mail from its own users (ask your admin). Failed checks are always flagged.
verified_risks_title: Before you turn on the badge
verified_risks_intro: The green badge can mislead you in these cases:
verified_risks_server: It's only reliable if your mail server adds its own check to all mail, including mail from its own users. Otherwise someone with an account on your server can make a fake email look verified. Ask your administrator.
verified_risks_old: Mail that arrived before your administrator set that up, and mail you imported (from another account or a backup), isn't protected and may show a badge it shouldn't.
verified_risks_meaning: “Verified” only means the email really comes from the domain after the @. It doesn't mean the sender is honest: paypa1.com, any Gmail account or a hacked account can be verified.
verified_risks_name: Look at the address, not the name: “PayPal” <someone@other.com> is verified for other.com, not for PayPal.
verified_risks_warnings: No warning doesn't mean the email is safe. And mailing lists or forwarded mail may show “Not verified” even when they're fine.

cal_new_share_added: {name} will get it when you create it
cal_error_new_share: It couldn't be shared like that, so it wasn't created. Check who you share it with.
cal_publish_warning: Anyone with the link can see every event in this calendar without signing in.
cal_subscribe_hint: Your calendar server downloads it and keeps it up to date; here it is read-only.
cal_subscribe_url_scheme: The address must start with https://, webcal:// or webcals://.
cal_subscribe_url_credentials: The address can’t contain a user name or password.
cal_unsubscribe_body: You’ll stop seeing its events. You can subscribe again at any time.
cal_trash_retention: Items here are deleted for good after {days} days.
privacy_direct_loaded_notice: These images came straight from the sender’s servers, as your settings say: the sender saw your IP address and when you opened this email. Trackers were removed first.
privacy_report_images_never: Your settings never load remote images, so the sender can’t tell you opened it.
privacy_report_images_direct: If you show them, they load straight from the sender, who will see your IP address and when you open it. Trackers are removed first.
privacy_report_images_direct_loaded: They loaded straight from the sender, who saw your IP address and when you opened it. Trackers were removed first.
privacy_report_images_proxy_loaded: They came through our proxy: the sender didn’t see your IP address.
settings_images_hint: Remote images can tell the sender when you open an email. “Ask” shows a button in each email. “Trusted senders” loads them at once from your contacts and from senders you chose with “Always from this sender” (never in Junk, nor when the sender check failed), and asks for the rest. Trackers are always removed first.
settings_images_forced: Your administrator blocks remote images for everyone.
settings_images_none: Remote images can’t be shown on this server: it has no image proxy and loading them from the sender isn’t allowed.
settings_images_via_hint: Through the proxy, the sender never sees your IP address. From the sender, the images come straight from the sender’s servers: the sender sees your IP address and when you open each email, and an email could make your browser call devices on your network (the router, a printer).
settings_images_proxy_only: Images always load through the proxy: your administrator doesn’t allow loading them from the sender, so the sender never sees your IP address.
settings_images_direct_auto: Load from the sender without asking
settings_images_direct_only: This server has no image proxy: images can only load straight from the sender’s servers, who will see your IP address and when you open each email; an email could also make your browser call devices on your network (the router, a printer). Off, every email asks first, with a warning; on, “Always” and trusted senders load at once.

match.countPlural=one: {count} sender trusted with “Always from this sender”
match.countPlural=other: {count} senders trusted with “Always from this sender”

compose_image_invalid: {name}: only PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP images up to 5 MB can go in the text
composer_plain_confirm_body: Formatting will be lost: bold, colours, fonts, links and images in the text. The words stay.
settings_compose_format_hint: Replies to plain-text messages start in plain text too. You can change it in each message (More options).
